title: ItemAbsence
description: Why one requested object did not arrive from a tier batch (`fetch_blobs`, `POST /eprfs/v1/blobs`, `/elohim/eprfs-blobs/1`): the typed reason inside `Unanswered<ItemAbsence>`, internally tagged by `kind` (kebab-case values, camelCase fields). `not-held` is an OBSERVED absence: with an empty `tried` it is a leaf store's own miss, with no tier dialled (B2); otherwise it is an absence at every tier listed in `tried`, in the order asked; `unreachable` and `membership-unknown` establish no absence (the chain advances to the next tier, and the walk reads them as withheld, never as not held); `refused` and `over-budget` are final for the item (a refusal does not fan out the read pattern; over budget is answered with its come-back time, not routed around); `integrity` means bytes failed their address and were never stored. In the batch route's absent trailer each entry is `{cid, path, unanswered}` with `unanswered` shaped by `$defs.UnansweredItemAbsence` (interfaces spec §A.6). Wire shape: this schema is the source of record; Rust mirror eprfs_core::ItemAbsence (elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/tier.rs, `#[non_exhaustive]`), with eprfs_core::ReachRefusal (reach.rs) for `refused`. That mirror's serde (tag `kind`, kebab-case tags, camelCase fields) is the encoding a TierEndpoint writes on the batch route, so it must serialize to this schema; no test pins the two yet (follow-on: an eprfs-serve contract test that serializes every variant and validates it here). Source of truth: the tier's answer to one batch request (Category C), never persisted.

items.description: A tier identity: `agent:<agent key>` when a cross-signed binding resolves one, else `transport:<peer id>` (the transport id the tier was dialled by). The indexical `own` is never serialized: eprfs-core's Serialize refuses it, every serving adapter stamps its own id, and a requester-side adapter rewrites a remote `own` to the dialled record's id (A2). Decides where to dial and what to count, never whom to credit (A11).

tried.description: Every tier asked, in order, by the ids the requester dialled. Empty for a leaf store's own miss, when no tier was dialled (B2; `ItemAbsence::not_held(vec![])`).

refusal.description: Reach said no, by name. To a requester outside reach, a missing object and a private one get the same refusal.
